Sixteenth Indian Expendition to Antarctica, Scientific Report, 2000 
Department of Ocean Development, Technical Publication No. 14 pp. 1 to 36 
Engineering and scientific activities / studies in Antarctica
PIYUSH KUMAR AND R.N.WAGHMARE
R & D E (Engrs.), Dighi, Pune - 411015
Abstract
An emergent requirement for a ne w water supply system circumventing
the use of MEG had to be  developed and installed at Indian  Antarctic Research
Station 'Maitri' taking into consideration the Methylene Ethylene Glycol mix-
ture leakage in the recent past which could pollute the Priyadarshini lake which
is a major source of water supply to the station.  So an alternative solution was
thought out by electrically heating the water supply line instead of conventional
water and MEG mixture heating arrangement. Also another emerging require-
ment was the shifting of power generation and supply system from inside of the
A-Block of the main Maitri station to outside which had to be developed and
installed at  Antarctica during XVI Indian Antarctic Expedition to meet the
demand of the station 'Maitri' taking into the past experience  of a fire accident.
Considering the Antarctic conditions, easy construction and transportability two
shelters of knock down type containerisied accommodation facility for the these
generator sets were made and installed at Antarctica. The main factor that affect
habitat construction in Antarctica are low temperature, high wind speeds, snow
accumulation and snow drift, local surface characteristics, visibility and accessi-
bility/inaccessibility. Also for disaster warning and regular maintenance of the
power supply systems, predictive analysis of generator sets through regular
data acquired from various vibration signatures was effectively carried out in
conjunction with R&DE(Engrs.) via e-mail.
Introduction
The Research & Development Establishment (Engineers), Pune is one of
the establishments under DRDO. The association of R&DE(Engrs.), Pune
with the Indian Antarctic Expeditions started from III Expedition when
indigenously manufactured structures /equipments were sent to Dakshin Gangotri
(DG) for trials in the extreme conditions of winter. Based on the feedback and
the requirements projected by the teams, further structures/equipments were
sent in the  subsequent expeditions with  further improvements and modifica-
tions. In continuation of the support, R&DE(Engrs.)  designed and constructed
Maitri, India's second permanent station during VII and VIII expeditions and a 
Power House in X expedition with fully indigenous material and equipments.
The generating sets were commissioned in XI expedition, however, due to a 
fire accident in the power house a new generating sets accommodation, Aditya,
was erected by XII expedition and Bhaskara by XIII expedition.
370
Piyush Kumar and R.N. waghmare 
Further to suffice the various requirements of the ongoing expeditions
R&DE(Engrs.) designed and constructed a Vehicle Repair Workshop Shelter
during XIII and XIV expeditions. The task of erection Balloon Launching Shel-
ter, developed and fabricated by R&DE(Engrs.) too was initiated in XIV expedi-
tion which further was continued in XV expedition. The Ice Core Drill Shelter
was erected in XV expedition which unpredictably met its misfortune and could
not be further be used.
Besides the various tasks of the XVI Expedition and XIV Wintering
Team, the major task was to construct a Medical Inspection Room capable of
accommodating all the facilities in A-Block.
Representative of R&DE(Engrs.) was assigned to provide technical
assistance and guidance to the Army Team in various tasks brought by XVI
expedition. He was also entrusted to carry out the scientific studies during
wintering period on the behavior of engineering material and the effect of Ant-
arctic environment on  foundation/repairs of life support systems/equipments.
Logistic Tasks
Safety Harnessing System for 28m Mast 
The 28 meter mast posed difficulties for easy climbing to facilitate the
scientific observations for National Physical Laboratory. So it was decided to
provide a safety harnessing system attached to the mast. This would provide a 
seating belt to a climbing person tied to a rope attached with a carabiner. This
system requires at least one person to operate. The person who is climbing when
feels tired can hang in air to rest for a while/to install his scientific equipments
in between, as the operator below locks him with the help of small push-pull lift
of 1.5 ton capacity with a simple handle. The same procedure can be followed
while descending too.
A proper site was chosen for installing the pulling clamp assembly with
SWR 9 mm dia x 120 m long steel rope wound on a steel reel. After installing
the fitment on the ground near the mast, pulleys were installed having checked
the vertical alignment. After examining thoroughly the problems at site, the
safety harnessing system was installed with a few modifications.
